prompt: State two fundamental differences between mass and weight.

mark_scheme.criterion: Mass is a scalar quantity (or measured in kg) whereas weight is a vector quantity (or measured in N).
Mass is an invariant property of a body (property resisting change in motion) whereas weight depends on the local gravitational field strength.

hints: Think about scalar vs vector nature and units.
Consider what happens to each quantity when moving to another planet.
solution: 1. Mass is a scalar quantity measured in kilograms, whereas weight is a vector quantity measured in newtons. 2. Mass is invariant everywhere, whereas weight varies with the local gravitational field strength.
teacher_walkthrough: Difference 1: Scalar vs vector nature (or SI unit kg vs N).
Difference 2: Mass is invariant; weight varies with local gravitational field strength g.
Award 1 mark for each clearly stated independent difference.
